passages.title: Bleeding
passages.text: Stop bleeding by pressing firmly and directly on the wound with a clean cloth, gauze or bandage, and keep pressing. Wear gloves or clean your hands first if you can. If blood soaks through, add more cloth on top instead of removing the first layer. Go to a health facility if the wound is deep or large, if the bleeding does not stop, or if it is a puncture wound such as from a nail.

passages.title: Cuts and wounds
passages.text: Once a small cut stops bleeding, rinse it under clean running water, wash it with soap and water, and cover it with a clean gauze pad or adhesive bandage. See a health worker if the wound is deep or large, keeps bleeding, or has a high risk of infection, such as a puncture from a nail or a wound from floodwater or an animal bite.

passages.text: Add what older adults and persons with disabilities need: extra maintenance medicine, eyeglasses, hearing-aid batteries, mobility aids and adult diapers. passages.text: If a person does not respond and is not breathing normally, call 911 and start CPR if you are trained: push hard and fast in the center of the chest, about 100 to 120 times a minute. If the person is breathing, turn them on their side in the recovery position and stay with them until help arrives.
